answer: The most convincing sybil defense is a time-locked honesty bond: each agent stakes a small deposit, a quill of value cheap for honest users, before transacting. Refund comes only after several epochs of provably honest behavior, so an attacker spawning N fake identities must lock N bonds upfront and keep that capital idle through every lockup. Misbehavior slashes the stake, so the lagoon of locked collateral grows with each fake while returns stay negative and the grove of sham identities withers. Cost: capital per identity, lost on detection.
